headline: Commission accepts funding and timeline plan to renovate Edmund Keefe Auditorium using Lake Street housing project proceeds
summary: The commission reviewed a plan to fund renovation of the Edmund Keefe Auditorium using proceeds from the Lake Street housing development, estimated at $18 million, plus additional fundraising to cover $29-34 million total renovation costs. The commission discussed project timing, phased construction, operating models, and governance, then voted to accept the plan as presented for an upcoming Aldermanic presentation.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 6, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Approved the auditorium funding and timeline plan as presented, 4-0.

plain_text:
Keefe Auditorium Commission 
 Friday, September 18, 2026 
City Hall, Room 208 
 
 
The Keefe Auditorium Commission met on the above date in Room 208 of City Hall, 
called to order by Chairman Dennis Schneider at 4:34pm.   In attendance were Shawn 
Smith, Dennis Schneider, Carl Dubois, and Daniel O’Donnell.  Also in attendance was 
Megan Caron.   
 
Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes 
 
Approval of Meeting Minutes of August 6, 2026. Motion by Carl Dubois, seconded by 
Shawn Smith to accept minutes. So Voted 4-0. 
  
MEETING OVERVIEW 
 
Chairman Schneider started the meeting by updating the commission on recent 
meetings with the mayor’s office, Alderman Dowd, Alderman Clemons and Tim 
Cummings.  Based on these discussions and past work by the Auditorium Commission, 
he prepared a power point presentation for the Aldermanic meeting scheduled for 
Tuesday, September 22, 2026.   See attached document entitled “Ensuing the Future of 
the Edmund Keefe Auditorium”. 
 
Funding Strategy and Financial Planning 
The main funding approach relies on leveraging proceeds from the Lake Street housing 
development project without additional city bonding or capital. 
• $18 million estimated renovation support from proceeds with no new city bonding. 
o Mayor and administration back using property development value to fund 
renovation. 
o No assumption of developer selection or finalized deal terms yet; figures 
remain preliminary. 
o Additional fundraising needed to cover gap between $18 million and $29–
34 million renovation cost estimates. 
o Operating expenses exceeding revenue will also require separate 
fundraising efforts. 
• TIF revenue expected to fund long-term debt service starting around October 
2030. 
o Bonding will be based on TIF revenue; no funds until tax increment revenue 
begins. 
o TIF funds will cover debt service over an extended period, not just initial 
years.
o Timing and amounts remain uncertain pending developer agreements and 
city negotiations. 
• Operating model options under consideration with preference toward an 
independent nonprofit. 
o For-profit operation run by Spectacle versus nonprofit theaters in the region 
discussed with city officials. 
o Mayor met with theater experts, leading to support for the nonprofit model. 
o This model aims for break-even operation and sustainable utilization post-
renovation. 
• Fundraising strategy to include hiring professional capital campaign experts 
o Commission recognizes need for professional fundraisers to meet $15 
million+ target. 
o Long timeline of 6+ years allows phased fundraising efforts. 
o Succession planning discussed given long project horizon and team 
member ages. 
Project Timeline and Development Phasing 
The project timeline spans from initial planning to reopening in 2032–2033, with phased 
construction aligned to developer progress. 
• Renovation start projected for October 2030 with reopening by October 2032–33 
o Timeline assumes waiting for TIF revenue and proceeds before renovation 
begins. 
o Earlier start possible if alternate funds become available. 
o Building mothballed and unusable for transition period starting around 2028. 
• Developer selection and detailed design phase expected to complete by 2028 
o Negotiations and housing agreement expected to take about 4 months after 
contract award. 
o Detailed design phase projected 12–16 months post-agreement, making 
project shovel-ready by late 2028. 
o Stabilization work on the existing building to occur during this period. 
• Phased construction approach encouraged to manage costs and fundraising 
o Options 2, 2a, and 2b from ICON are preferred; Option 1 considered 
insufficient. 
o Phasing could enable earlier partial opening with subsequent expansions. 
o Phased plan expected to reduce upfront fundraising pressure and attract 
incremental funding. 
• Transition period plan needed to support users during building closure from ~2028 
to 2032 
o Planning for community and performance groups’ relocation during 
unusable period is critical.
o Potential to use classrooms and portable buildings as temporary 
operational spaces during construction. 
o User outreach and involvement recommended to maintain engagement 
through transition. 
Architectural and Construction Considerations 
Design focus is on achieving a viable lobby addition and functional renovation while 
preserving operational flexibility. 
• Lobby addition on south side prioritized to improve facility functionality. 
o Current ICON plans lack a south lobby; work needed to create phased 
designs including this feature. 
o Classrooms at the back and other spaces could be repurposed during 
construction. 
o Cost implications of phasing acknowledged but considered acceptable for 
long-term benefit. 
• Utilities and structural planning linked to developer’s infrastructure work 
o Utility connections likely to come from Lake Street side; coordination critical 
to avoid duplication. 
o Potential synergy if utility conduits serve both housing and auditorium 
projects. 
o Construction sequencing to include building firewalls and sound walls for 
separation. 
• Mothballing costs include sprinkler system and heating per fire department 
requirements. 
o Early proceeds could fund installing essential safety systems to reduce 
mothballing expenses. 
o Sprinklers and electrical upgrades needed to keep building safe during 
dormancy. 
o Use of building during partial construction possible if safety needs met. 
• Salvage and asset recovery during demolition discussed as fundraising 
opportunity. 
o Some auditorium items (plaques, doors) reserved; other building materials 
may be sold. 
o City’s Amy DeRoche manages disposition of surplus items; coordination 
needed to maximize returns. 
o Prior examples show potential to raise funds from reusable assets. 
Governance, Stakeholder Engagement, and Organizational Planning 
Clear communication, leadership continuity, and stakeholder involvement are essential 
for project success.
• Commission seeks definitive guidance from aldermen and city administration. 
o Presentation planned to clarify options, costs, and timeline for aldermen to 
avoid premature objections. 
o Emphasis on transparency and managing expectations around bonding and 
tax impact. 
o Opportunity for commissioners to provide feedback before formalizing 
plans. 
• Succession and capacity planning critical due to long project duration. 
o Commission members acknowledge likelihood of turnover before project 
completion. 
o Need to recruit and engage new talent to support fundraising and project 
management. 
o Current members willing to lead fundraising but require broader team 
involvement. 
• User engagement and expert advisory panels recommended. 
o Theater experts involved in utilization planning to ensure sustainable 
operations. 
o Involving current user groups in maintenance and programming during 
transition. 
o Regular communication to maintain community support and involvement. 
• City administration actively supports and coordinates with external stakeholders. 
o Mayor and administration backing critical to advancing legislation and 
developer selection. 
o Ongoing dialogue with aldermen to build consensus and address concerns. 
o Public meetings planned to keep transparency and update community. 
 
Motion by Daniel O’Donnell, seconded by Carl Dubois, to accept the plan as 
presented (see attachment).   So voted 4-0. 
 
Next Meeting: Thursday, October 1, 2026 at 4:30pm in room 208 of City Hall. 
 
Motion to adjourn by Shawn Smith, seconded by Daniel O’Donnell.   Meeting 
adjourned at 5:23 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, Shawn M. Smith, Auditorium Commission Secretary 
 
Attachments 
(1) Powerpoint Presentation for Planned Aldermanic Meeting of September 22, 
2026, “Ensuring the Future of the Edmund Keefe Auditorium”
